The assigned head adds the 24-hour, build/Go-version, wall, and toolchain-void checks, but the certificate parser still accepts any nonempty `cert=` (`cmd/nova-pulse/accept.go:424`). The spec says `cert=<id>` is the first 12 hex of the record SHA-256; this code computes a separate raw-file ID for void/control use without checking the embedded ID. Changing only `at=`/`until=` while leaving `cert=` unchanged can therefore extend a certificate and pass the freshness checks, bypassing §2 rule 6. Define a non-self-referential canonical ID (for example, hash the normalized record with `cert=` omitted), validate it before accepting the record, and add a regression that extends the timestamps without updating the ID and expects `bench-uncertified`.
